product_name: Symantec SWG (Symantec Edge SWG, Symantec Cloud SWG)
product_brief: Secure Web Gateway providing centralized enforcement and quantum-ready security at the network edge.
pqc_capability_description: Supports Module Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) hybrid key exchange methods, such as X25519MLKEM768. Implements quantum-safe key exchange at the proxy layer to strengthen encryption transparently without requiring changes to end users or endpoint devices.
crypto_primitives: X25519, ML-KEM (Module Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism)
key_management_model: Hybrid key exchange at the proxy layer
pqc_roadmap_details: Supports incremental adoption of PQC using hybrid methods (X25519MLKEM768) to maintain compatibility with existing environments while aligning with emerging cryptographic standards.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Low friction; enables incremental adoption without disruptive rip-and-replace initiatives; maintains compatibility with existing applications and infrastructure; no changes required for end users or endpoint devices.

product_brief: Network switch providing quantum-safe secure boot using LDWM hash-based signatures.
pqc_capability_description: Provides quantum-safe secure boot using LDWM hash-based signatures (HBS), a precursor to NIST approved LMS. New quantum-safe editions of Secure Boot and Cisco Trust Anchor Technologies implementing new NIST PQC standards are expected in late 2025 or 2026.
pqc_roadmap_details: New quantum-safe editions of Secure Boot and Cisco Trust Anchor Technologies implementing new NIST PQC standards are expected in late 2025 or 2026. Availability of products utilizing standard industry components (CPUs/TPMs) may be delayed until late 2026 or 2027.
signature_schemes: LDWM hash-based signatures (HBS); planned NIST PQC standards (specific algorithms not named for the switch, though ML-DSA is mentioned generally for PKI).

product_brief: A solution for continuous cryptographic discovery, risk assessment, and transition to post-quantum cryptography.
pqc_capability_description: Provides continuous discovery of cryptographic assets, risk assessment for HNDL attacks, and remediation via configuration guidance for PQC/Hybrid-PQC algorithms. Includes a Cipher Translation Proxy that reencrypts vulnerable traffic into quantum-safe standards (such as ML-KEM) in real-time for legacy systems.
crypto_primitives: ML-KEM (mentioned as a quantum-safe standard for reencryption); deprecated OpenSSL versions (mentioned as context for discovery).
architecture_type: Central nervous system for cryptographic posture; acts as a proxy (Cipher Translation Proxy) at the network edge; ingests telemetry from PAN-OS NGFW and Prisma Access.
fips_validated: Not stated (mentions mapping against FIPS 140-3 standards, but does not state the product itself is validated)
primary_platforms: PAN-OS NGFW, Prisma Access, SIEM, EDR, CMDB, asset management platforms, network clouds, log platforms.
pqc_roadmap_details: Generally available January 30, 2026; additional integration enhancements planned for April 2026.
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Yes; provides real-time Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM), continuous discovery of applications/devices/IoT, analysis of traffic metadata (protocols, key exchange, algorithms, hashes, certificates), and detection of deprecated cryptographic libraries (e.g., OpenSSL).
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Yes; supports discovery of IoT devices and provides Cipher Translation Proxy for legacy/IoT devices that cannot be upgraded.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Supports structured migration (Current State to Quantum Ready to Quantum-Safe); offers agentic remediation and proxy-based translation to avoid code changes; integrates with existing infrastructure to reduce operational friction.

product_brief: All-domain quantum-resistant encryption solution validated across air, land, sea, and space.
pqc_capability_description: Isidore Quantum is an all-domain quantum-resistant encryption solution validated across air, land, sea, and space. It is built on NSA frameworks with patented AI enhancements, including real-time machine learning. It combines CNSA Suite 2.0 compliance with zero-trust, AI-enhanced encryption, eliminating legacy PKI and key management infrastructure. It has been field-tested with U.S. military branches and deployed on a SpaceX mission.
target_industries: Government, Defense, Private sectors, SCADA, Telecom, Aerospace, Finance
regulatory_status: FIPS 140-3 compliance, ITAR and EAR exemptions authorized for export, CNSA Suite 2.0 compliance
testing_&_validation_methods: Field-tested with U.S. Air Force, Army, Navy, and Space Force; deployed aboard Rogue Space’s Barry CubeSat on SpaceX’s Transporter-13 mission.

product_brief: Integrates network intelligence and quantum security via built-in QKD board for NetEngine 8000E routers.
pqc_capability_description: The document describes Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) integration, not Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms. It mentions mitigating quantum security threats via QKD, but does not state support for PQC algorithms (e.g., CRYSTALS-Kyber, Dilithium).
key_management_model: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) integration; built-in QKD board inserted into router; integrates quantum, negotiation, and communication channels.
architecture_type: Built-in QKD board integrated into NetEngine 8000E series router; inline integration into existing network infrastructure.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: Built-in QKD board; high-precision noise reduction algorithm integrating quantum, negotiation, and communication channels into one fiber; eliminates need for standalone QKD devices.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Slashes overall investment cost by over 60%; eliminates need for additional devices or optical fibers; simplifies architecture.
financial_&_business_impact: Slashes overall investment cost by over 60%; device expenses and optical fiber installations previously consumed over 60% of total investment cost.
